conclusion.summary: Full fresh review of the three-file capability-grant diff against AC-1 to AC-8 and R01 to R03; all eight criteria are satisfied. One deeply frozen CAPABILITY_GRANT_GRAMMAR is the single source of truth, with EXTERNAL_READ_GRAMMAR and MODEL_CLASS_GRAMMAR as aliases of its subtrees, and the schema is pinned by exact deep equality to a pure projection of it. The schema requires all ten always-emitted properties, including requestedModelClass, and closes the top-level object and allowedExternal. Channel selection keeps request-over-instance precedence while routing every defined source through assertChannelType, which raises a controlled PolicyError invalid_channel_type for any value that is not a non-empty primitive string; the validated value is the emitted one, so no non-string channel reaches allowedOutputChannels. Schema and runtime agree on string arrays, canonicalized external-read domains, GET-only methods, model class, modelPolicy enums with open extras, booleans, approval identifiers and output channels. External-read, model-class and deep-immutability behavior stays green, with one necessary tightening: an invalid pack modelPolicy.default is no longer masked by a valid request model class, since it would otherwise be emitted and rejected by the new enum. The dependency-free harness accepts six representative compiled grants and rejects missing-required, extra-property, wrong-type, bad-method, bad-model-class, malformed-array and channel negatives. Exactly the three allowed files change, npm test passes 48 of 48, and git diff --check is clean. Three pre-existing nits remain and block nothing: an unused cloneAndFreezeJsonObject helper, a generically named hand-rolled validator that ignores unsupported JSON Schema keywords, and a self-referential external-read branch in the grammar equality test. Observation only, not an acceptance decision.

criteria_coverage.notes: CAPABILITY_GRANT_GRAMMAR is a single deeply frozen export created with deepFreeze; EXTERNAL_READ_GRAMMAR and MODEL_CLASS_GRAMMAR are aliases of its subtrees rather than parallel definitions, and DEFAULT_MODEL_CLASS now reads from it. Test 2 pins the on-disk schema by exact deep equality to a projection built only from grammar values, so the grammar is the single source of truth for the complete grant contract.

The schema required list now holds all ten always-emitted properties, adding requestedModelClass, privateDataTouched and requiresApproval; top-level additionalProperties flips from true to false and allowedExternal is closed with required readDomains and readMethods. The compiled grant emits exactly those ten keys, and tests 25 and 26 exercise each missing-required key and both extra-property cases.

selectOutputChannelType routes every defined source through assertChannelType, which throws PolicyError invalid_channel_type unless the value is a primitive string of non-zero length, and returns the validated value that is then frozen into allowedOutputChannels. Only the absent-source fallback bypasses it, and it returns the literal cli. The corpus in tests 19 and 20 covers null, true, false, 0, array, object, boxed String and empty string from both request and instance sources, so no non-string or empty channel can be emitted.

Property-by-property agreement holds: runId and packSlug are guarded by assertPrimitiveString; allowedTools and allowedPaths are string arrays; allowedOutputChannels is exactly one non-empty string; readDomains carry the same three canonical patterns the runtime tests with and are lowercased, IPv6-canonicalized, deduplicated and sorted; readMethods are GET-only, unique and capped at one; requestedModelClass and modelPolicy.default share the local and cloud enum; modelPolicy stays open to extra keys, matching cloneAndFreezeJsonLike; privateDataTouched is boolean; requiresApproval is a unique array capped at two over exactly the two identifiers the runtime pushes.

External-read normalization, canonicalization, GET-only denial and controlled PolicyError behavior are unchanged (tests 21, 22, 23, 34, 35), model-class precedence and fallback are unchanged (tests 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14), and detached deep immutability of grant fields still holds (tests 36, 37). One behavior deliberately tightens: an invalid pack modelPolicy.default is no longer masked when the request supplies a valid class, because cloneAndFreezeModelPolicy would otherwise emit that value into a modelPolicy that the new enum rejects. Test 8 was rewritten to assert the new controlled rejection, which is required for AC-2 and AC-4 consistency rather than a regression.

The harness uses only node:test, node:assert/strict, node:fs and node:path, with no new dependency, and is deterministic: fixed fixtures, no clock or randomness. Test 24 validates six representative compiled grants covering local, cloud, cloud with private data, external send, canonicalized external read and pack-default fallback. Tests 25 to 29 cover every missing-required key, extra top-level and extra allowedExternal keys, non-GET method, invalid model classes for both requestedModelClass and modelPolicy.default, wrong primitives, and malformed arrays including empty, over-length, empty-string and duplicate channel and approval cases.

Test 2 asserts strict deep equality of the parsed on-disk schema against expectedCapabilityGrantSchema, which is assembled purely from grammar values, and applies assertDeepFrozen recursively to the whole grammar. Test 24 applies the same recursive freeze check to every representative compiled grant, and test 36 additionally proves the grant fields are detached from their inputs. The vacuous externalRead pattern comparisons recorded as a nit reduce the strength of one branch but do not remove either the equality or the freezing proof.

changed-paths.json lists exactly the three allowed files and the diff touches nothing else. npm test passes 48 of 48 with 0 failures and git diff --check exits 0 with empty output. The diff adds no dependency, no import beyond node built-ins already in use, no network call, no commit and no external transfer; base and head commits are identical, so the change is an uncommitted working-tree diff.

fingerprint.normalized_title: hand rolled partial json schema validator named generically

findings.rationale: validateAgainstSchema and collectSchemaErrors at test/policy.test.js:210-216 implement only type, enum, pattern, minLength, maxLength, oneOf, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, items, required, properties and additionalProperties. Any keyword outside that subset, for example $ref, allOf, anyOf, not, const, dependentRequired or prefixItems, is silently skipped rather than reported as unsupported, while the generic name reads like a general JSON Schema validator. For the sealed capability-grant schema the supported subset is exactly the keyword set the schema actually uses, so the harness is sound today and AC-6 holds; the exposure is future drift, where a newly added keyword would be ignored and a negative fixture could pass unnoticed.
findings.suggested_remediation: Rename the helper to something scope-explicit such as validateAgainstSupportedSchemaSubset, and make collectSchemaErrors push an error when it meets a keyword outside its supported set so schema growth cannot silently outrun the harness.
findings.title: Generically named validateAgainstSchema silently ignores unsupported JSON Schema keywords

location.symbol: capability-grant grammar is deeply frozen and schema exactly matches it

findings.rationale: In the grammar equality test the expected externalRead branch is built from EXTERNAL_READ_GRAMMAR.dnsNamePattern, ipv4Pattern and ipv6Pattern at test/policy.test.js:477-479, and src/core/policy.js:60 defines EXTERNAL_READ_GRAMMAR as an alias of CAPABILITY_GRANT_GRAMMAR.externalRead. Those three comparisons therefore assert a value against itself and cannot fail, so that part of the literal is vacuous rather than a pin. The three regex bodies are still independently pinned by the separate agent-pack externalRead subtree test, and the sibling methods, modelClass, modelPolicy, grant, outputChannels, allowedExternal and approval entries are compared against real literals, so AC-1 and AC-7 remain covered; the defect is only the missing independent restatement of the pattern strings.
findings.suggested_remediation: Restate the three expected pattern strings as literals in the grammar equality test, or derive them from the independently built pattern bodies, so the assertion pins the regexes instead of comparing the grammar to itself.
